name: Pustulosis palmaris et plantaris

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical diagnosis of Pustulosis palmaris et plantaris

criteria.description: Presence of sterile pustules localized on the palms and/or soles persisting for more than 3 months
Symmetrical involvement of palms and/or soles with erythematous scaling plaques
Negative bacterial and fungal cultures from pustular lesions
Histopathological findings consistent with pustular psoriasis (intraepidermal pustules with neutrophilic infiltration)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of chronic sterile pustules on palms and/or soles with typical lesion distribution and exclusion of infectious causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by histopathology and exclusion of infection.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Sterile pustules localized on palms and soles
searchTerms: pus-filled bumps on hands and feet
sterile pustules on palms and soles
non-infected pustules on hands and feet

pathognomonic.symptomName: Erythematous scaling plaques on palmar and plantar surfaces
searchTerms: red scaly patches on palms and soles
flaky red skin on hands and feet
scaly plaques on palmar and plantar surfaces

common.symptomName: Pruritus of affected palmar and plantar skin
searchTerms: itchy skin on palms and soles
pruritus of hands and feet skin
itching in affected hand and foot areas

common.symptomName: Pain and tenderness on palms and soles
Fissuring and cracking of palmar and plantar skin
searchTerms: cracked skin on hands and feet
fissures in palmar and plantar skin
skin splits and cracks on palms and soles

occasional.symptomName: Nail changes including pitting and onycholysis

rare.symptomName: Development of pustular psoriasis at other body sites
searchTerms: psoriasis with pustules at other sites

rare.symptomName: Systemic symptoms such as low-grade fever

laboratory: Negative bacterial and fungal cultures from pustules
Elevated inflammatory markers (ESR, CRP) in some cases
imaging: X-rays may show joint changes if psoriatic arthritis develops

distinguishingFeatures: Lack of sterile pustules and typical histology
Pustules resolve with treatment of infection

redFlags: Rapid progression of pustules with systemic symptoms
Signs of secondary bacterial infection (e.g. purulence, fever)
Development of psoriatic arthritis with joint deformity
